chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan ibn Yahya from Murra, the freedman of Khalid, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who throws off the louse, so he said: 'Throw it off, may God Almighty distance it, [it is] not blameworthy and not lost.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on removing lice while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a person in *ihram* may remove lice without incurring penalty, distinguishing this minor act from the prohibition of removing hair or nails. The phrase 'not blameworthy' (*ghayr mahmuda*) indicates that while permissible, it is not an act of great virtue, whereas 'not lost' (*la mafquda*) confirms that the louse's removal does not count towards the specific prohibitions regarding the loss of body parts. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (*rukhas*) in ritual purity, ensuring that minor nuisances do not burden the pilgrim.
